content.value_statement: MSBuild and package version rules are easy to miss during .NET repository changes. This skill runs a focused architecture linter and explains the violations to fix.
actual_capabilities: Runs the configured .NET architecture linter from the repository root.
Reports rule-based violations for MSBuild and Central Package Management files.
Flags hardcoded package versions in Directory.Packages.props.
Checks Version.props import ownership and consumer symlink expectations.
Detects PackageReference version attributes in project files.
Provides variable naming guidance for unknown package version entries.
limitations: Requires the lint-dotnet.sh helper script to exist under the plugin root.
Uses local shell execution and needs permission to inspect the workspace.
Covers only the listed MSBuild and package-management rules.
Does not replace dotnet build, test, or security dependency scanning.

use_cases.title: Review package version hygiene
use_cases.description: Check a .NET repository for hardcoded package versions and CPM violations before a merge.

use_cases.title: Validate shared MSBuild infrastructure
use_cases.description: Confirm that Version.props imports appear only in approved owner files.

use_cases.title: Prepare release cleanup
use_cases.description: Run the linter before release branching and convert findings into focused remediation work.

prompt_templates.title: Run the linter
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for the current repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use lint-dotnet to run the .NET architecture linter on this repository. Summarize any violations and the recommended fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check package version rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of Central Package Management
prompt_templates.prompt: Run lint-dotnet and focus on package version findings. Explain which files need CPM or Version.props changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a remediation plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn lint results into work items
prompt_templates.prompt: Run lint-dotnet, group the findings by rule, and create a prioritized remediation plan with owners and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a migration branch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before a repository-wide MSBuild change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use lint-dotnet to audit this migration branch. Compare the findings with the intended MSBuild and CPM architecture rules, then identify any release blockers.

output_examples.input: A repository contains hardcoded package versions in package management files.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the affected files, explains why the versions violate CPM rules, and recommends moving them to named version variables.

output_examples.input: A project file includes package versions directly on package references.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the project files, explains the CPM conflict, and recommends removing direct version attributes.

output_examples.input: A repository has no matching architecture violations.
output_examples.output: The skill reports that the configured lint rules passed and that no remediation is needed for these checks.

best_practices: Run the skill from the repository root so path-based rules resolve correctly.
Review the helper script before first use in a community skill installation.
Pair lint results with build and test runs before merging architecture changes.
anti_patterns: Do not run the shell command automatically in untrusted repositories.
Do not treat clean lint output as proof that builds or tests pass.
Do not edit Version.props ownership rules without confirming the repository architecture.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It checks selected .NET MSBuild, Version.props, and Central Package Management architecture rules.

faq.question: Does it run code locally?
faq.answer: Yes. It runs a bash helper script from the plugin root against the current repository.

faq.question: Can it fix violations automatically?
faq.answer: The skill describes fixes, but users should review and apply changes according to repository policy.

faq.question: Does it replace dotnet build?
faq.answer: No. It checks architecture rules and should be used alongside normal build and test commands.

faq.question: Which package management style does it support?
faq.answer: It focuses on Central Package Management patterns using Directory.Packages.props and Version.props.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is most useful for .NET developers, build engineers, and release teams maintaining shared MSBuild rules.
